correctness.rationale: For each selected rook cell x, a failure to see a distance-two cell is exactly the presence of a three-edge path in the selected row-column bipartite graph. P4-free bipartite graphs are star forests. Distinct nontrivial components cannot be joined without creating P4. An isolated vertex on each side makes any forest nonmaximal; a one-sided isolate forces all opposite-side degrees one and all active same-side degrees >=2, and these constraints suffice. This proves three disjoint families. The labeled-star component EGF and restricted Stirling partitions enumerate them with exact edge weights; the minimum multiplicities follow from covering all vertices of each part. Small boundaries m=n=2 and m=2,n>=2 are explicit. A separate direct-pairwise geodesic verifier tested 108688 subsets on eleven boards, and 121 m,n pairs for symbolic checks. Finite experiments are support, not proof.

value.rationale: The complete maximal-set size distribution for an unrestricted two-parameter family is a natural invariant describing all terminal outcomes of greedy outer visibility/general-position selection. The 2025 visibility-polynomial inclusion-exclusion theorem specifically motivates knowledge of maximal sets. The formula separates spanning star-forest and asymmetric one-sided-isolate saturation, counts exactly how many distinct worst-case minimum-size terminal sets exist, and exhibits arbitrarily long internal spectrum gaps through \(M_{2,n}(z)=nz^2+2^nz^n\). This is not just the known minimum/maximum cardinality or a relabeling of all-subset counting.
